games.note: Clemson is 5-3 and Syracuse is 4-4, and both are just hanging on in my others receiving votes. The loser probably falls off the list.
The Holy War. Utah is 8-0 and still only No. 15 in my poll. Beating a 7-1 BYU team makes that spot a lot harder to defend.
UCLA is 8-0 and I still dropped them to No. 14. A noon kickoff in Minneapolis against a Minnesota team that already beat Iowa is a real test.
Both teams are 6-2. Texas climbed 10 spots this week, and a road win in Columbia would show the jump was earned.
A 5-3 South Carolina team at No. 7 is the call in my poll I'll hear the most about. Texas A&M is 4-4 with nothing to lose and every reason to make me look bad.
Oregon got back into the conversation by beating Northwestern. Ohio State is coming off a loss and can't afford a third.
Penn State is 4-4 and barely holding onto votes. Washington is 5-3 and not much safer. Whoever loses is out of the picture.
My No. 2 against my No. 3 in Baton Rouge, both 6-2. The winner has the best argument for being the team chasing Georgia.
No. 8 vs. No. 9, and Kentucky has the better record at 7-1. Neyland at night is where that record gets tested.
Miami is 8-0 and the only unbeaten team in my top five. I dropped Notre Dame 11 spots without them losing, so this is their chance to prove me wrong.
Iowa beat Wisconsin to get back into my poll. Northwestern lost at Oregon and needs this one to stay in the conversation.
My No. 1 goes on the road to Oxford at night. Ole Miss is 6-2, and this is its best shot at a statement win all year.
Texas Tech is back in my poll at No. 19 after beating Arizona. A 5-3 West Virginia team in a late kickoff is the definition of a trap game.
